notes: [VCov]: line, branch and toggle definitions, the toggle exclusions (task or begin/end locals, leading underscore, integers, over 256 bits, with --coverage-max-width and --coverage-underscore), per-parameter-set counting, edges near time zero with the advice to zero coverage before reset release, the UNOPTFLAT over-count, and the $stop rule (Suppressing Coverage) are each on the page as the document says. The page says a coverage_off/coverage_on metacomment pair disables and enables coverage around a block, which is why the document's advice not to hide a gap with coverage_off is the document's inference and not the page's.

[VCovExe]: --annotate marks a line with % when all points are below --annotate-min (default 10), '-' marks a point below the min under --annotate-points, --report summary and hier are in the usage list, and the page tells a reader to remove conditions that never occur with $stop or coverage_off. The closing line of the document, that point counts show whether new stimulus reached new points, is a reading of --report and --rank, not stated in those words; inference-level and fair.

[OTDV]: the code metrics (line, toggle, FSM state and transition, conditional, branch), toggle closed on the IO ports only, code coverage not a verdict (the AND-gate example: 100 percent code coverage does not say the design works), and the exclusion rules (designer sign-off in a PR review; annotation of ALL exclusions; categories UNR, NON_RTL, UNSUPPORTED, EXTERNAL, LOW_RISK; the explanation mandatory for the last three, as the document says) are on the page. Imprecision: the document says OpenTitan 'records every exclusion with a category tag'; the page says annotations 'can be prefixed' with a category tag and that exclusions 'almost always' fall in those categories, and requires an annotation for every exclusion. A fair summary, slightly stronger than the page.

Branch points: the page for Arguments says --coverage-line covers basic blocks and branches of if/else are covered separately with --coverage-branch, and the gate's build asks for line and toggle only (eda.py:595). tests/test_coverage_read.py runs the real build on Verilator 5.052 and asserts branch 100.0, so the data holds branch points from that build; the document's hedge, 'branch percentages come from whatever points the data holds', is the correct reading, and a requirement's branch bound is met only if the installed Verilator emits them.

Version: the manual text read is 5.054; the repository's CI uses apt Verilator 5.020 and the local one is 5.052 (eda.py comment at COVERAGE_MAIN), so a reader on 5.020 should expect small differences. The document's [VCov] statements are the long-standing ones.

gate_claims.claim: coverage.read builds with Verilator --coverage-line and --coverage-toggle (line and toggle only), runs the testbench, then verilator_coverage reads the data
the data is written back with verilator_coverage --write and an lcov report with --write-info
branch percentages in the result come from whatever points the data holds (the type is the point's t key; the build does not ask for branch)
the simulation is judged first as simulator.run judges it (one verdict with the run's nonce, no failed check) and, if it fails, coverage is not read
only points in the design files count; the default design is every source except the file that declares the top module
a design parameter names the design files; each must be among the sources
none of the design files may declare the top module (the testbench is never measured)
a percentage is points hit at least once over all points, rounded down to two places, so it never rounds up into a bound
a design file with no coverage point at all fails the run
no source may use $fopen, $system, $c or DPI, the testbench included

a source that is not a design file may not carry a Verilator configuration (`verilator_config), an include, or a coverage_off or coverage_block_off pragma; design files may (run locally: a testbench with coverage_off or coverage_block_off is refused, a design file with coverage_off is accepted) (the code is at lines 513, 552-553)

the gate matches coverage_off and coverage_block_off only and does not match coverage_on: a testbench carrying coverage_on alone is accepted (run locally), and so is a design file carrying coverage_on; a lone coverage_on turns nothing off, so the reason the gate gives holds
the gate refuses coverage_off only outside design files, so a gap hidden in a design file is not caught
the gate sets no threshold; a requirement's bounds on line, toggle and branch are checked after a passing run
a bound on a metric the run did not report fails (so a branch bound needs branch points in the data)
the tool is available, so the document opens with Practising
the skill holds coverage.read, which is AVAILABLE
a testbench that exercises the design meets the bounds and an idle one fails them, with branch points in the data from the real Verilator build
a testbench that could forge the counts ($c, $fopen, DPI, coverage_off, an include, a verilator_config) is refused
